statements.t: We intend to accomplish this goal in part by investing in our specialized and higher-value specialty alcohol production and distribution infrastructure, expanding production in high-demand essential ingredients, expanding and extending the sale of our products into new regional and international markets, building efficiencies and economies of scale and capturing a greater portion of the value stream.

Although we expect domestic sales to remain the more attractive option through the end of 2026, we are beginning to see more compelling economics for resuming renewable fuel exports to Europe in 2027.
At our Pekin dry mill, the debottlenecking project we completed in the second quarter is performing in line with our plan following the restart of the facility.

We remain on target to increase the dry mill’s annual production capacity by approximately 8%, or 5 million gallons, allowing us to exit 2026 at our new targeted annual run rate of approximately 65 million gallons.

At our Pekin Campus, the first phase of our barge dock project, which added a new liquid loadout, is complete and operational, and we expect to complete the second phase, consisting of improvements to the existing dock, by the end of 2026.
We expect these investments to provide greater logistics flexibility and loading capacity while helping us better leverage the strategic value of our Pekin location.

At our Columbia facility, we expect to complete the installation of a third CO 2 storage tank before the end of 2026, providing additional capacity to capture more of our existing CO 2 production and to serve the growing demand for liquid CO 2 in the Pacific Northwest.
We remain on track to qualify 90 million gallons or more of combined production for Section 45Z tax credits in 2026.

As a result of our efforts to lower our carbon intensity scores, we now project our Columbia facility to qualify for $0.30 per gallon and our Pekin dry mill to qualify for $0.20 per gallon, in each case on a gross credit basis.

Accordingly, we now expect to generate a minimum of $20.0 million of Section 45Z tax credit earnings, net of estimated monetization costs, in 2026, compared to our previously expected minimum of $15.0 million.
This expected minimum does not include any incremental Section 45Z tax credit earnings from low carbon intensity corn supplied by farmers under our cooperative agreements described below.
We expect the earnings contribution from this first agreement to be modest in 2026, but to build in 2027 as participating farmers adopt additional measures beginning this fall.

In addition, at our Columbia facility, we are completing the first phase of an energy reduction project in the fourth quarter of 2026 to further lower the facility’s carbon intensity score and support our Section 45Z earnings initiatives.
Over the past twelve months, we have reduced our term debt by $30.0 million, which we expect will lower our debt servicing costs by approximately $4.3 million annually.
In the near term, our capital allocation priority is high-return projects that expand capacity and improve efficiencies.
Longer term, we intend to pursue additional ways to monetize our CO 2 revenue stream relative to alternatives.
We believe we are well positioned to benefit from favorable industry fundamentals, and we are executing plans to grow, drive profitability and build shareholder value.

We believe that our critical accounting estimates, defined as those estimates that we believe are the most important to the portrayal of our financial condition and results of operations and that require management’s most difficult, subjective or complex judgments, often as a result of the need to make estimates about the effects of matters that are inherently uncertain, are the impairment of long-lived assets…

For the three- and nine-month periods in 2026, we recorded no provision for income taxes because we expect to use a portion of our net operating loss carryforwards to offset taxable income for the year.

As of September 30, 2026, we had $25.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, $42.7 million of unused borrowing availability under Kinergy’s operating line of credit and $65.0 million that may be available for capital improvement projects under our Orion term loan.

We expect to sell these Section 45Z tax credits in the first half of 2027, and we expect the proceeds to provide an additional source of liquidity to strengthen our balance sheet and fund growth investments.

We believe we have sufficient liquidity to meet our anticipated working capital, debt service, capital expenditure and other liquidity needs for at least the next twelve months from the date of this report.
As of September 30, 2026, we had future commitments for certain capital projects totaling $15.2 million.

We currently expect total capital expenditures of approximately $25.0 million for 2026, which includes maintenance projects and more than $10.0 million of high-return projects to expand production capacity and improve efficiencies, such as the debottlenecking project at our Pekin dry mill, improvements to our barge dock at our Pekin Campus and an additional CO 2 storage tank at our Columbia facility.
We expect to fund these expenditures with cash on hand and cash generated from our operations.
Sales of our common stock under the Sales Agreement, if any, will be made through sales deemed to be an “at the market offering” as defined in Rule 415(a)(4) under the Securities Act.
We will pay the applicable sales agent a commission of 3.0% of the gross proceeds from each sale.
We intend to use the net proceeds from any sales for general corporate purposes, including working capital and capital expenditures.

statements.t: We also continued to execute on our high return capital projects to expand production capacity, improve process efficiencies and optimize CO 2 .”
